questions.question:
How many of the following items are ADDED (credited) while computing the amount due to the executors of a deceased partner?
(i) His share of general reserve
(ii) Interest on his drawings up to the date of death
(iii) His share of gain on revaluation
(iv) His share of profit up to the date of death
(v) His drawings up to the date of death
(vi) Interest on his capital up to the date of death
questions.explanation:
(i) Added: accumulated profits belong to all partners.
(ii) Deducted: interest on drawings is charged to the partner.
(iii) Added: a revaluation gain is shared in the old ratio.
(iv) Added: profit for the intervening period.
(v) Deducted: drawings reduce the claim.
(vi) Added: interest on capital is allowed to the partner.
Items added: (i), (iii), (iv) and (vi), which is 4 items.
Answer: (3)

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the accounting aspects that arise on the retirement or death of a partner?
options: Ascertainment of new profit sharing ratio and gaining ratio
Adjustment in respect of unrecorded assets and liabilities
Settlement of the amount due to the retired or deceased partner
Bringing in of premium for goodwill in cash by the outgoing partner
questions.explanation:
Step 1: NCERT's list of accounting aspects on retirement or death includes the following:
- new and gaining ratios
- goodwill and revaluation
- unrecorded items
- accumulated profits and losses
- profit up to the date of retirement or death
- adjustment of capital
- settlement of the amount due
Step 2: Options (1), (2) and (3) all appear in this list.
Step 3: Premium for goodwill is brought in by an incoming partner on admission. An outgoing partner receives his share of goodwill; he does not bring in a premium.
Answer: (4)

questions.question:
Prem, Quasim, Raj and Sahil share profits in the ratio 2 : 3 : 1 : 4. Quasim retires, and his share is acquired by Prem and Raj in the ratio 2 : 1.
Statement I: The new profit sharing ratio of Prem, Raj and Sahil is 2 : 1 : 2.
Statement II: Sahil's capital account will be debited with a part of Quasim's share of goodwill, because Sahil continues in the firm.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Quasim's share is $\frac{3}{10}$.
Prem acquires $\frac{2}{3}\times\frac{3}{10}=\frac{2}{10}$, so his new share is $\frac{2}{10}+\frac{2}{10}=\frac{4}{10}$.
Raj acquires $\frac{1}{10}$, so his new share is $\frac{1}{10}+\frac{1}{10}=\frac{2}{10}$.
Sahil stays at $\frac{4}{10}$, so the new ratio is 4 : 2 : 4 = 2 : 1 : 2. Statement I is correct.
The gaining ratio is 2 : 1 : 0. Sahil neither gains nor sacrifices, so he bears no goodwill. Statement II is incorrect.
Answer: (2)

questions.question:
Statement I: Goodwill already appearing in the books at the time of a partner's retirement is written off by debiting all partners' capital accounts, including the retiring partner's, in the old profit sharing ratio.
Statement II: In the absence of any agreement, under Section 37 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, an outgoing partner may choose either interest @ 6% p.a. till the date of payment or the share of profits earned with his money.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation:
Statement I is true. Existing goodwill belongs to all the old partners, so it is written off in the old ratio, as in the Hanny–Pammy–Sunny illustration.
Statement II is true. Section 37 gives the outgoing partner exactly this option: interest @ 6% p.a., or the share of profit earned with his money (based on capital ratio).
Answer: (1)

questions.question:
Case: Pawan, Qasim and Rekha share profits in the ratio 3 : 2 : 1. Qasim dies on September 30, 2024, and the books close on March 31. The deed provides the following:
- Qasim's capital on April 1, 2024 is Rs. 1,00,000.
- Interest on capital is allowed at 6% p.a.
- A salary of Rs. 1,500 per month is payable to Qasim; it has not been paid for the current year.
- His share of profit up to death is based on the average profit of the last three years. Those profits were Rs. 80,000, Rs. 90,000 and Rs. 1,00,000.
- Goodwill is valued at 2 years' purchase of the same average profit.
- General Reserve stands at Rs. 36,000.
- Qasim's drawings up to death were Rs. 18,000.
What is the amount payable to Qasim's executors?
questions.explanation:
Given: Qasim's share = 2/6. Average profit = 2,70,000/3 = 90,000.
Goodwill = 2 × 90,000 = 1,80,000, so his share = 60,000.
Profit up to death = 90,000 × 6/12 × 2/6 = 15,000.
Interest on capital = 1,00,000 × 6% × 6/12 = 3,000.
Salary = 1,500 × 6 = 9,000. Reserve share = 36,000 × 2/6 = 12,000.
Total = 1,00,000 + 12,000 + 60,000 + 15,000 + 3,000 + 9,000 − 18,000 = Rs. 1,81,000.
Option (2) leaves out the salary. Option (3) takes the profit share for 12 months instead of 6.
Answer: (1)

questions.question:
Match List-I (situation on retirement) with List-II (journal entry):
List-I
A. Whole amount due is treated as a loan
B. Interest on the retiring partner's loan becomes due
C. An instalment is paid to the retiring partner
D. Retiring partner is paid in full by cheque
List-II
(i) Retiring Partner's Loan A/c Dr. To Bank A/c
(ii) Interest A/c Dr. To Retiring Partner's Loan A/c
(iii) Retiring Partner's Capital A/c Dr. To Retiring Partner's Loan A/c
(iv) Retiring Partner's Capital A/c Dr. To Bank A/c
questions.explanation:
A: Transferring the whole amount to the loan account debits Capital and credits Loan, which is (iii).
B: Interest increases the amount owed, so Interest A/c is debited and the Loan A/c is credited, which is (ii).
C: Paying an instalment reduces the loan, so Loan A/c is debited and Bank A/c is credited, which is (i).
D: Full payment debits Capital and credits Bank directly, which is (iv).
Answer: (1)

questions.question: On Sheela's retirement, it was agreed that expenses owing, shown at Rs. 4,500, should be brought down to Rs. 3,750. Which entry is correct?
options: Revaluation A/c Dr. 750 To Expenses Owing A/c 750
Expenses Owing A/c Dr. 750 To Revaluation A/c 750
Expenses Owing A/c Dr. 3,750 To Revaluation A/c 3,750
Revaluation A/c Dr. 3,750 To Expenses Owing A/c 3,750
questions.explanation:
The liability falls by Rs. 4,500 − Rs. 3,750 = Rs. 750.
A decrease in a liability is a gain to the firm.
So the liability account is debited and Revaluation A/c is credited with Rs. 750.
Options (3) and (4) use the revised balance instead of the change. Option (1) treats the decrease as a loss.
Answer: (2)

questions.question: Ravi retires from a firm. The partnership deed is silent on how the amount due to him will be settled, and the firm cannot pay him immediately. Under Section 37 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, what is Ravi entitled to until the amount is paid?
options: Interest at 12% p.a. on the amount due
Either interest at 6% p.a. on the amount due, or the share of profits earned with his money (based on capital ratio), at his option
A share of future profits in his old profit sharing ratio
Only the amount due, without any interest or share of profits
questions.explanation:
Section 37 applies when there is no agreement about settling the outgoing partner's dues.
Under it, the outgoing partner may choose either interest at 6% p.a. till the date of payment, or the share of profits earned with his money, which is based on the capital ratio.
Option (1) is wrong because the rate is 6%, not 12%.
Option (3) is wrong because the profit share is linked to his money (capital ratio), not to his old profit sharing ratio.
Option (4) ignores the right Section 37 gives him.
Answer: (2)

Read the two statements about a retirement where goodwill already appears in the books.
Statement I: The existing goodwill is written off by debiting all partners' capital accounts, including the retiring partner's, in the old ratio.
Statement II: The retiring partner's share of the current value of goodwill is then credited to him by debiting the continuing partners' capital accounts in their new profit sharing ratio.
options: Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect and Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct: book goodwill belongs to all the old partners, so it is written off in the old ratio.
Statement II is incorrect: the retiring partner is compensated by the partners who gain, in their gaining ratio, not their new ratio. For example, in Hanny–Pammy–Sunny the new ratio was 2 : 1 but the gaining ratio was 1 : 1.
Answer: (1)

questions.question: Asha died on June 30. Under the partnership deed, her share of profit for the intervening period is to be calculated on the basis of sales. Last year's sales were Rs. 10,00,000 and profit was Rs. 1,50,000. Sales from April 1 to June 30 were Rs. 2,40,000. Asha's share of profit was 1/4. What amount will be credited to Asha's Capital Account by debiting Profit and Loss Suspense Account?
questions.explanation:
Given: last year's sales Rs. 10,00,000; profit Rs. 1,50,000; sales up to death Rs. 2,40,000; Asha's share 1/4.
Rate of profit on sales = 1,50,000 / 10,00,000 = 15%.
Profit up to death = 2,40,000 × 15% = Rs. 36,000.
Asha's share = 36,000 × 1/4 = Rs. 9,000.
Rs. 9,375 would come from the time basis (3/12 of last year's profit), which the deed does not allow here.
Answer: (3)

questions.question: On the death of a partner, goodwill is to be valued at 3 years' purchase of the average profits of the last four years. The profits were Rs. 40,000, Rs. 50,000, Rs. 60,000 and Rs. 50,000. What is the value of the firm's goodwill?
questions.explanation:
Given: profits of 4 years = Rs. 2,00,000 in total; 3 years' purchase.
Formula: Goodwill = Average profit × Number of years' purchase.
Average profit = Rs. 2,00,000 ÷ 4 = Rs. 50,000.
Substituting: Goodwill = Rs. 50,000 × 3.
So goodwill = Rs. 1,50,000.
Answer: (1)

questions.question: Xavier, Yash and Wasim are partners. Xavier and Yash share profits in the ratio of 3 : 4 between themselves. Wasim retires. After all adjustments for reserves and revaluation, the balance in Wasim's Capital Account is Rs. 84,000. Xavier and Yash agree to pay him Rs. 1,05,000 in full settlement, and their own ratio stays unchanged. What amount will Xavier's Capital Account be debited with for hidden goodwill?
questions.explanation:
Given: adjusted balance Rs. 84,000; lump sum paid Rs. 1,05,000.
Formula: Hidden goodwill = Amount paid − Amount due.
Hidden goodwill = 1,05,000 − 84,000 = Rs. 21,000.
The gaining ratio equals the old ratio 3 : 4, so Xavier's debit = 21,000 × 3/7 = Rs. 9,000.
Rs. 12,000 is Yash's debit, not Xavier's.
Answer: (4)

questions.question: Xavier, Yash and Zoya share profits in the ratio 6 : 2 : 2. Yash retires, and Xavier and Zoya will share future profits equally. Goodwill, not in the books, is valued at Rs. 1,00,000. Which is the correct journal entry for goodwill?
options:
Xavier's Capital A/c Dr. 15,000; Zoya's Capital A/c Dr. 5,000
To Yash's Capital A/c 20,000

Zoya's Capital A/c Dr. 30,000
To Yash's Capital A/c 20,000
To Xavier's Capital A/c 10,000

Xavier's Capital A/c Dr. 10,000; Zoya's Capital A/c Dr. 10,000
To Yash's Capital A/c 20,000

Zoya's Capital A/c Dr. 20,000
To Yash's Capital A/c 20,000
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Xavier's change = $\frac{5}{10}-\frac{6}{10}=-\frac{1}{10}$. This is a sacrifice.
Step 2: Zoya's change = $\frac{5}{10}-\frac{2}{10}=\frac{3}{10}$. This is a gain.
Step 3: Zoya is debited $1{,}00{,}000 \times \frac{3}{10}$ = Rs. 30,000.
Step 4: She compensates Yash with $\frac{2}{10}$ = Rs. 20,000 and Xavier with $\frac{1}{10}$ = Rs. 10,000.
Step 5: Option (4) ignores Xavier's sacrifice.
Answer: (2)

questions.question: On the retirement of a partner, the new share of each continuing partner is calculated as:
options: Old share + Share acquired from the outgoing partner
Old share − Share acquired from the outgoing partner
Old share × Share acquired from the outgoing partner
questions.explanation:
A continuing partner keeps his own share. He also gets whatever part of the outgoing partner's share he takes over.
So, New share = Old share + Acquired share.
Option (c), New share − Old share, is the formula for the gaining share, not the new share.
Subtracting or multiplying the shares has no basis.

questions.question: The amount due to the executors of a deceased partner is not paid in full on the date of death. In the Balance Sheet of the reconstituted firm, where is the unpaid balance of the Executor's Account (or Executor's Loan Account) shown?
options: On the assets side as a fictitious asset
On the liabilities side until the last instalment is paid
As a deduction from the capitals of the surviving partners
It is not shown, because it is settled outside the books
questions.explanation:
The amount payable to the executors is a debt the firm owes to an outsider. This is the same as a retiring partner's loan.
NCERT notes that such a loan balance appears on the liabilities side of the Balance Sheet until it is fully paid.
It is neither an asset nor a reduction of the surviving partners' capitals.

questions.question: On the retirement of a partner, the net profit on revaluation of assets and liabilities is transferred to:
options: the continuing partners' capital accounts in their new profit sharing ratio
the continuing partners' capital accounts in their gaining ratio
all partners' capital accounts, including the retiring partner's, in their old profit sharing ratio
the retiring partner's capital account only
questions.explanation:
The change in the values of assets and liabilities took place while the retiring partner was still a member of the firm.
So the gain or loss belongs to all partners, including the retiring one.
It is shared in the old profit sharing ratio.
The gaining ratio (option 2) is used for goodwill, not for revaluation.

questions.question: Case: Dev, Esha and Farhan were partners. Farhan retired, and the amount due to him, Rs. 70,000, was paid in full through the bank. Before any payment, the firm's bank balance was Rs. 12,000. The capital of the new firm was fixed at Rs. 1,50,000, with Dev and Esha sharing in the ratio 3 : 2. After all adjustments, Dev's capital stood at Rs. 95,000 and Esha's at Rs. 52,000. Any excess capital was withdrawn and any deficiency was brought in through the bank. Any shortfall in bank is met by an overdraft. What amount of bank overdraft will appear in the Balance Sheet of the reconstituted firm?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Required capitals: Dev = $1,50,000 \times \frac{3}{5}$ = Rs. 90,000. Esha = Rs. 60,000.
Step 2: Dev withdraws 95,000 − 90,000 = Rs. 5,000. Esha brings in 60,000 − 52,000 = Rs. 8,000.
Step 3: Bank = 12,000 + 8,000 − 5,000 − 70,000 = −Rs. 55,000.
Step 4: The negative balance is a bank overdraft of Rs. 55,000, shown on the liabilities side.
Rs. 58,000 ignores the capital adjustments. Rs. 61,000 reverses the inflow and outflow.
Answer: (1)

questions.question: Aman, Bharat and Charu share profits in the ratio 5 : 4 : 3. Bharat retires, and Aman and Charu decide to share future profits in the ratio 3 : 2. Goodwill is valued by agreement at Rs. 1,80,000 and is not in the books. With what amount will Aman's capital account be debited for goodwill?
questions.explanation:
Given: Goodwill = Rs. 1,80,000. Bharat's share = $\frac{4}{12}$, so his share of goodwill = Rs. 60,000.
Step 1: Aman's gain = $\frac{3}{5}-\frac{5}{12}=\frac{36-25}{60}=\frac{11}{60}$.
Step 2: Charu's gain = $\frac{2}{5}-\frac{3}{12}=\frac{24-15}{60}=\frac{9}{60}$.
Step 3: Gaining ratio = 11 : 9.
Step 4: Aman's debit = $60{,}000 \times \frac{11}{20}$ = Rs. 33,000. Charu's debit is Rs. 27,000.
Step 5: Rs. 36,000 wrongly uses the new ratio; Rs. 37,500 wrongly uses the old ratio.
Answer: (1)

Assertion (A): On the retirement of a partner, the General Reserve appearing in the Balance Sheet is credited to the capital accounts of all partners, including the retiring partner, in the old profit sharing ratio.
Reason (R): Accumulated profits were earned while all the old partners were in the firm, so they belong to all of them.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:

R is true. NCERT states that accumulated profits belong to all the partners, and the retiring partner is entitled to his share.

questions.question:
Arun, Bina and Chetan share profits in the proportion of $\frac{1}{2}$, $\frac{3}{10}$ and $\frac{1}{5}$. Bina dies. As agreed, Arun takes $\frac{1}{3}$ of her share and Chetan takes the remaining part.
Statement I: The new profit sharing ratio of Arun and Chetan is 3 : 2.
Statement II: The gaining ratio of Arun and Chetan is the same as their old ratio, i.e., 5 : 2.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Arun acquires $\frac{1}{3} \times \frac{3}{10} = \frac{1}{10}$. Chetan acquires $\frac{2}{3} \times \frac{3}{10} = \frac{2}{10}$.
New shares: Arun = $\frac{5}{10} + \frac{1}{10} = \frac{6}{10}$. Chetan = $\frac{2}{10} + \frac{2}{10} = \frac{4}{10}$. So the new ratio is 3 : 2, and Statement I is correct.
The gaining ratio is the ratio of acquired shares: $\frac{1}{10} : \frac{2}{10}$ = 1 : 2, not 5 : 2. So Statement II is incorrect.
The gaining ratio equals the old ratio only when the share is taken in the old ratio, which is not the case here.
Answer: (3)

Reason (R): The Employees' Provident Fund is an amount the firm owes to its employees, so it is a liability and not an accumulated profit.

Lata and Mehul agree to pay him Rs. 1,05,000 in full settlement and continue to share profits in their old ratio. By what amount will Lata's capital account be debited for Nikhil's hidden goodwill?

(ii) If the continuing partners acquire the outgoing partner's share in their old ratio, their gaining ratio is the same as their old ratio.
(iii) If the continuing partners agree on a specified new ratio, that ratio must still be worked out by adding acquired shares to old shares.

questions.question: Ravi, Sohan and Tarun are partners. Tarun dies in the middle of the accounting year. His share of profit from the date of the last Balance Sheet to the date of his death is to be credited to him through a suspense account, without closing the books. Which journal entry records this?
options: Profit and Loss Suspense A/c Dr. To Tarun's Capital A/c
Tarun's Capital A/c Dr. To Profit and Loss Suspense A/c
Profit and Loss A/c Dr. To Tarun's Executor's A/c
Ravi's and Sohan's Capital A/c Dr. To Profit and Loss A/c
questions.explanation:
The deceased partner has earned a share of profit for the intervening period, so the amount must be credited to his capital account.
The books are not closed, so a Profit and Loss Suspense A/c is debited in its place.
The entry is therefore: P&L Suspense A/c Dr. To Tarun's Capital A/c.
Option (2) reverses the entry. It would reduce Tarun's claim, not record his share of profit.
Answer: (1)

questions.question:
How many of the following items are ADDED while computing the amount due to a retiring partner?
(i) Credit balance of his current account
(ii) His share of goodwill
(iii) His drawings up to the date of retirement
(iv) His share of gain on revaluation
(v) Interest on his drawings up to the date of retirement
(vi) Salary due to him up to the date of retirement
questions.explanation:
(i) Added: a credit balance of the current account is owed to him.
(ii) Added: he receives his share of goodwill.
(iii) Deducted: drawings reduce his claim.
(iv) Added: he gets his share of revaluation gain.
(v) Deducted: interest on drawings is charged to him.
(vi) Added: salary due is payable to him.
So items (i), (ii), (iv) and (vi) are added, which makes 4.
Answer: (3)

questions.question:
Case: Anu, Bina, Chetan and Dev share profits in the ratio of 3 : 3 : 2 : 2. Bina retires. Anu, Chetan and Dev decide to share future profits in the ratio of 2 : 2 : 1. Goodwill of the firm is valued at ₹1,50,000. Goodwill does not appear in the books.
Consider the following statements:
(i) Dev neither gains nor sacrifices on Bina's retirement.
(ii) The gaining ratio of Anu and Chetan is 1 : 2.
(iii) Anu's capital account will be debited with ₹15,000 for Bina's share of goodwill.
(iv) Dev's capital account will be debited with ₹9,000, since he continues in the firm.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation:
Old shares are Anu 3/10, Chetan 2/10 and Dev 2/10. New shares are Anu 4/10, Chetan 4/10 and Dev 2/10.
(i) Correct: Dev's gain is 2/10 − 2/10 = 0.
(ii) Correct: Anu gains 1/10 and Chetan gains 2/10, so the ratio is 1 : 2.
(iii) Correct: Bina's goodwill share = 1,50,000 × 3/10 = ₹45,000. Anu pays 1/3 of it, which is ₹15,000, and Chetan pays ₹30,000.
(iv) Incorrect: Dev has no gain, so he does not compensate Bina at all.
Answer: (3)

questions.question: The amount due to the executors of a deceased partner was Rs. 60,000. Rs. 20,000 was paid immediately. The balance is to be paid in 4 equal half-yearly instalments of principal, plus interest at 10% p.a. on the outstanding balance. What is the total amount paid to the executors with the SECOND half-yearly instalment?

Interest for the second half-year = 30,000 × 10% × 6/12 = Rs. 1,500.
Second instalment = 10,000 + 1,500 = Rs. 11,500.

questions.question: Gita, Hari and Ishaan share profits in the ratio 3 : 3 : 2. Hari retires, and Gita and Ishaan agree to share future profits equally. What is the gaining ratio of Gita and Ishaan?
questions.explanation:
Formula: Gaining share = New share − Old share.
Step 1: Gita's gain = $\frac{1}{2} - \frac{3}{8} = \frac{1}{8}$.
Step 2: Ishaan's gain = $\frac{1}{2} - \frac{2}{8} = \frac{2}{8}$.
Step 3: Gaining ratio = 1 : 2. The gains add up to $\frac{3}{8}$, which is Hari's share, so the working checks.
Step 4: 3 : 2 is wrong. Old ratio cannot be used because the new ratio is specified.
Answer: (1)

questions.question:
Assertion (A): When a partner retires, his share of the General Reserve shown in the Balance Sheet is credited to his capital account.
Reason (R): Accumulated profits belong to all the partners who were in the firm when they were earned, so they are distributed among all partners in the old profit sharing ratio.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Before the firm is reconstituted, the General Reserve is transferred to the capital accounts of all partners, including the retiring partner. The entry is: Reserve A/c Dr. To All Partners' Capital A/cs.
R is true. Accumulated profits were earned while every old partner was in the firm, so the old ratio is used to share them.
R explains A. The retiring partner gets credit because he is one of the partners entitled to these profits.
Answer: (1)

questions.question: On the retirement of a partner, the balance sheet shows a debit balance in the Profit and Loss Account. Which journal entry records its treatment?
options: Profit and Loss A/c Dr. To All Partners' Capital A/cs
Remaining Partners' Capital A/cs Dr. To Profit and Loss A/c
All Partners' Capital A/cs Dr. To Profit and Loss A/c
Retiring Partner's Capital A/c Dr. To Profit and Loss A/c
questions.explanation:
A debit balance in the Profit and Loss Account is an accumulated loss.
Every partner, including the retiring partner, must bear this loss in the old ratio.
To close the debit balance, the capital accounts are debited and the Profit and Loss A/c is credited: All Partners' Capital A/cs Dr. To Profit and Loss A/c.
Option (1) is the entry for accumulated profits, not losses.
Options (2) and (4) leave out some of the partners who must share the loss.
Answer: (3)

questions.question:
A, B and C share profits in the ratio of 5 : 3 : 2. C retires. On that date C's capital account shows a credit balance of Rs. 50,000. The balance sheet also shows:
Reserve Fund Rs. 60,000
Employees' Provident Fund Rs. 10,000
Profit and Loss Account (debit balance) Rs. 20,000
What will C's capital account show after adjusting only these items?
questions.explanation:
Given: C's share = $\frac{2}{10}$. Opening capital = Rs. 50,000.
Reserve Fund: C is credited 60,000 × $\frac{2}{10}$ = Rs. 12,000.
P&L debit balance: C is debited 20,000 × $\frac{2}{10}$ = Rs. 4,000.
Employees' Provident Fund is a liability, so there is no adjustment.
So C's capital = 50,000 + 12,000 − 4,000 = Rs. 58,000.
Rs. 60,000 wrongly treats the EPF as a reserve, and Rs. 62,000 ignores the loss.
Answer: (4)

His share of profit on revaluation of assets and liabilities

Assertion (A): On retirement, the retiring partner is entitled to a share of the firm's goodwill.
Reason (R): The goodwill has been earned by the firm through the efforts of all the existing partners, including the retiring partner.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false

questions.question: Ravi, Sunil and Tara share profits in the proportion of $\frac{2}{5}$, $\frac{2}{5}$ and $\frac{1}{5}$. Ravi retires. He surrenders $\frac{1}{4}$ of his share in favour of Sunil and the rest in favour of Tara. The new profit sharing ratio of Sunil and Tara is:
questions.explanation:
Given: Ravi's share is $\frac{2}{5}$. Sunil gets $\frac{1}{4}$ of it and Tara gets $\frac{3}{4}$ of it.
Sunil acquires $\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{2}{5} = \frac{1}{10}$. Tara acquires $\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{2}{5} = \frac{3}{10}$.
New shares: Sunil = $\frac{4}{10} + \frac{1}{10} = \frac{5}{10}$. Tara = $\frac{2}{10} + \frac{3}{10} = \frac{5}{10}$.
So the new ratio is 1 : 1. Option (c), 1 : 3, is only the ratio in which they acquire Ravi's share.
Answer: (2)

Reason (R): Closing the books and preparing final accounts for such a short intervening period is considered cumbersome.

Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

R is true. NCERT says it is considered cumbersome to close the books and prepare final accounts for that period.
R gives the very reason why such estimates are used, so it correctly explains A.

questions.question: Kiran, whose share of profit is $\frac{1}{4}$, retires from a firm. His adjusted capital balance is Rs. 62,000, and the continuing partners settle his claim by paying a lump sum of Rs. 80,000. On the basis of this payment, what is the implied value of the goodwill of the whole firm?
questions.explanation:
Given: lump sum = Rs. 80,000; adjusted capital = Rs. 62,000; Kiran's share = $\frac{1}{4}$.
Kiran's hidden goodwill = Rs. 80,000 − Rs. 62,000 = Rs. 18,000.
This amount is $\frac{1}{4}$ of the firm's goodwill, so Firm's goodwill = Rs. 18,000 ÷ $\frac{1}{4}$.
So the firm's goodwill = Rs. 72,000. Rs. 18,000 is only Kiran's share, not the firm's total.
Answer: (1)

questions.question:
Case: Prakash, Qadir and Rohit share profits in the ratio 3:2:1. Qadir died on September 30, 2024. On April 1, 2024 his capital was Rs. 50,000, and the Balance Sheet showed a General Reserve of Rs. 30,000. The agreement with his executors provides:
(i) Goodwill is valued at 2 years' purchase of the average profit of the last 3 years. These profits were Rs. 36,000, Rs. 48,000 and Rs. 60,000.
(ii) His share of profit up to the date of death is based on last year's profit of Rs. 60,000.
(iii) Interest on capital is allowed at 10% p.a.
(iv) The revaluation of assets showed a loss of Rs. 6,000.
Qadir's drawings up to the date of death were Rs. 4,000.
The amount transferred to Qadir's Executor's Account will be:
questions.explanation:
Qadir's share = 2/6 = 1/3.
Goodwill: average profit = 1,44,000/3 = 48,000; goodwill = 48,000 × 2 = 96,000; his share = 32,000.
Reserve share = 30,000 × 1/3 = 10,000.
Profit for 6 months = 60,000 × 6/12 × 1/3 = 10,000.
Interest on capital = 50,000 × 10% × 6/12 = 2,500.
Credits = 50,000 + 32,000 + 10,000 + 10,000 + 2,500 = 1,04,500.
Deductions: drawings 4,000 + revaluation loss share (6,000 × 1/3) 2,000 = 6,000.
Balance transferred to Executor's A/c = Rs. 98,500. Option (2) ignores the deductions.
Answer: (1)

questions.question: Goodwill does not appear in the books. A partner retires. Which of the following statements regarding the treatment of his share of goodwill is INCORRECT?
options: The retiring partner's capital account is credited only with his share of goodwill, not with the full goodwill of the firm.
The gaining partners' capital accounts are debited individually.
When the new profit sharing ratio is specified, each continuing partner's gain is found as new share minus old share.
The continuing partners always compensate the retiring partner in their new profit sharing ratio.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: the retiring partner's capital is credited only with his share of goodwill.
(2) Correct: the gaining partners are debited individually.
(3) Correct: gaining share = new share − old share.
(4) Incorrect: compensation is made in the gaining ratio, not the new ratio. The two ratios coincide only in special cases. For example, the Keshav-Pankaj case gives a gaining ratio of 13:11 although the new ratio is 5:3.
Answer: (4)

questions.question:
How many of the following statements about settling a retiring partner's dues are correct?
(i) Without an agreement, the outgoing partner may claim interest @ 6% p.a. till the date of payment.
(ii) The share of profits option under Section 37 is based on the profits earned with his money, i.e. the capital ratio.
(iii) The entries for interest on the loan and for payment of an instalment are repeated each year till the loan is paid off.
(iv) The retiring partner's loan account is closed as soon as the first instalment is paid.
(v) When an instalment is paid, the retiring partner's loan account is credited.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: Section 37 allows interest @ 6% p.a.
(ii) Correct: the profit share is linked to the use of his money, i.e. the capital ratio.
(iii) Correct: both entries are repeated until the loan is cleared.
(iv) Incorrect: the balance remains until the last instalment is paid.
(v) Incorrect: paying an instalment debits the loan account (Loan A/c Dr. To Bank A/c).
So 3 statements are correct.
Answer: (2)

The goodwill of the firm is valued at Rs. 90,000, and no goodwill account is to be raised. Which journal entry correctly adjusts Lalit's share of goodwill?
options: Kavya's Capital A/c Dr. Rs. 15,000; Manav's Capital A/c Dr. Rs. 15,000; To Lalit's Capital A/c Rs. 30,000
Kavya's Capital A/c Dr. Rs. 22,500; Manav's Capital A/c Dr. Rs. 7,500; To Lalit's Capital A/c Rs. 30,000
Manav's Capital A/c Dr. Rs. 30,000; To Lalit's Capital A/c Rs. 30,000
Kavya's Capital A/c Dr. Rs. 45,000; Manav's Capital A/c Dr. Rs. 45,000; To Lalit's Capital A/c Rs. 90,000

Gaining share = New share − Old share.
Kavya: $\frac{1}{2}-\frac{3}{6}=0$. She neither gains nor sacrifices.
Manav: $\frac{1}{2}-\frac{1}{6}=\frac{2}{6}$. He gains the whole of Lalit's share.
Lalit's goodwill share = $90{,}000\times\frac{2}{6}$ = Rs. 30,000.
So only Manav's capital is debited. Option (2) wrongly uses the old ratio 3 : 1.

questions.question: After a partner retires, the capital of continuing partner Mohit, after all adjustments, exceeds his share of the agreed new capital. The excess is withdrawn in cash. Which journal entry records this?

Pallavi, Qasim and Rekha share profits in the ratio 4 : 1 : 3. Qasim retires, and Pallavi and Rekha decide to share future profits in the ratio 1 : 3. Goodwill of the firm is valued at Rs. 96,000 and is not shown in the books. Consider the following statements:
(i) Rekha's capital account is debited with Rs. 36,000.
(ii) Pallavi's capital account is credited with Rs. 24,000.
(iii) Qasim's capital account is credited with Rs. 12,000.
(iv) Pallavi's capital account is debited because she is a continuing partner.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: Pallavi's change = $\frac{2}{8}-\frac{4}{8}=-\frac{2}{8}$, a sacrifice. Rekha's change = $\frac{6}{8}-\frac{3}{8}=\frac{3}{8}$, a gain.
(i) Correct: Rekha is debited $96{,}000 \times \frac{3}{8}$ = Rs. 36,000.
(ii) Correct: Pallavi is credited for her sacrifice, $96{,}000 \times \frac{2}{8}$ = Rs. 24,000.
(iii) Correct: Qasim is credited $96{,}000 \times \frac{1}{8}$ = Rs. 12,000.
(iv) Incorrect: Pallavi sacrificed, so she is credited, not debited.
So 3 statements are correct.
Answer: (3)

questions.question: Pari, Qadir and Ruchi are partners sharing profits in the ratio of 3 : 2 : 1. Qadir retires, and the goodwill of the firm is valued at Rs. 1,20,000. Pari and Ruchi agree to share future profits in the ratio of 2 : 3. Goodwill is not to appear in the books. By what amount will Ruchi's Capital Account be debited in the goodwill adjustment entry?

Given: old ratio 3:2:1, new ratio 2:3, goodwill Rs. 1,20,000.
Formula: Gain = New share − Old share.
Pari: $\frac{2}{5}-\frac{1}{2}=-\frac{1}{10}$, so Pari sacrifices.
Ruchi: $\frac{3}{5}-\frac{1}{6}=\frac{13}{30}$, so Ruchi gains.
Substituting: Ruchi's debit = $\frac{13}{30}\times 1,20,000$ = Rs. 52,000.
This amount is credited to Qadir (Rs. 40,000) and Pari (Rs. 12,000).
So Ruchi is debited Rs. 52,000. Rs. 40,000 is wrong because Ruchi must also compensate Pari for her sacrifice.
Answer: (1)

questions.question:
Statement I: When the new profit sharing ratio of continuing partners is specified, each partner's gaining share is found by deducting his old share from his new share.
Statement II: When goodwill does not appear in the books, the retiring partner's capital account is credited with the full value of the firm's goodwill.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Gaining share = New share − Old share. NCERT applies this whenever the new ratio is specified, as in the Keshav–Pankaj case giving 13 : 11.
Statement II is incorrect. The retiring partner is credited only with his own share of goodwill, that is, the firm's goodwill × his old share. He is not credited with the whole value.
Answer: (2)

questions.question: Xavier, Yamini and Zoya share profits in the proportion of $\frac{2}{5}$, $\frac{1}{3}$ and $\frac{4}{15}$. Xavier retires. He surrenders $\frac{1}{4}$ of his share in favour of Yamini and the remaining share in favour of Zoya. What will be the new profit sharing ratio of Yamini and Zoya?
questions.explanation:
Given: Xavier's share = $\frac{2}{5}$.
Yamini acquires $\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{2}{5} = \frac{1}{10}$, and Zoya acquires $\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{2}{5} = \frac{3}{10}$.
Yamini's new share = $\frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{10} = \frac{13}{30}$.
Zoya's new share = $\frac{4}{15} + \frac{3}{10} = \frac{8}{30} + \frac{9}{30} = \frac{17}{30}$.
So the new ratio is 13 : 17. The option 1 : 3 is the gaining ratio, and 17 : 13 reverses the order.
Answer: (3)

Gajender would get Rs. 24,000 and Harinder Rs. 12,000, so options (1) and (2) are other partners' shares.
So Inder's capital account is credited with Rs. 36,000.

Read the following statements.
Assertion (A): When a partner retires and the firm gives no information about how his share is to be taken over, the continuing partners share future profits in their old ratio between themselves.
Reason (R): In the absence of any agreement, the continuing partners are presumed to acquire the outgoing partner's share in their old profit sharing ratio.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT gives an example: when Deepti retires from a 3 : 2 : 1 firm, Asha and Nisha share profits 3 : 1.
R is true. Without information, the outgoing share is assumed to be taken in the old ratio.
R explains A. If the outgoing share is taken in the old ratio, each continuing partner's share grows in the same proportion. So their old ratio stays unchanged.

Arun, Bina and Chetan share profits in the ratio 2 : 2 : 1. Bina retires on March 31, 2024. On that date the following information is available:
- Bina's capital account (credit): Rs. 80,000
- Bina's current account (credit): Rs. 6,000
- General Reserve: Rs. 50,000
- Profit on revaluation: Rs. 15,000
- Goodwill of the firm: Rs. 75,000 (not appearing in the books)
- Bina's drawings not yet adjusted: Rs. 12,000
What is the amount due to Bina?
questions.explanation:
Given: Bina's share = 2/5.
Formula: Amount due = capital + current account credit + share of reserve + share of revaluation profit + share of goodwill − drawings.
Shares:
- Reserve: 50,000 × 2/5 = 20,000
- Revaluation profit: 15,000 × 2/5 = 6,000
- Goodwill: 75,000 × 2/5 = 30,000
Substituting: 80,000 + 6,000 + 20,000 + 6,000 + 30,000 − 12,000 = 1,30,000.
So the amount due = Rs. 1,30,000. Option (4) wrongly credits the whole goodwill of the firm instead of her share.
Answer: (1)

questions.question:
A, B and C share profits in the ratio of 3 : 2 : 1. Match each situation in List-I with the new profit sharing ratio of the continuing partners in List-II.
List-I
(A) A retires (no agreement)
(B) B retires (no agreement)
(C) C retires (no agreement)
(D) A retires and B and C take over his share equally
List-II
(i) 3 : 1
(ii) 7 : 5
(iii) 2 : 1
(iv) 3 : 2
questions.explanation:
(A) A retires, so B : C continue in their old ratio, 2 : 1, which is (iii).
(B) B retires, so A : C = 3 : 1, which is (i).
(C) C retires, so A : B = 3 : 2, which is (iv).
(D) Each of B and C gets $\frac{1}{2} \times \frac{3}{6} = \frac{3}{12}$.
B's new share = $\frac{4}{12} + \frac{3}{12} = \frac{7}{12}$. C's new share = $\frac{2}{12} + \frac{3}{12} = \frac{5}{12}$. So the ratio is 7 : 5, which is (ii).
Answer: (1)

questions.question: Arjun, Bela and Charu share profits in the ratio of 5 : 3 : 2. Bela retires. After all adjustments, the capital balances are Arjun Rs. 75,000, Bela Rs. 90,000 and Charu Rs. 45,000. The new ratio of Arjun and Charu is 3 : 2. It is decided that the amount payable to Bela will be brought in by Arjun and Charu so that their capitals become proportionate to the new ratio. How much cash will Charu bring in?
questions.explanation:
Given: the continuing partners' capitals are Rs. 75,000 and Rs. 45,000, Rs. 90,000 is payable to Bela, and the new ratio is 3 : 2.
Total capital of the new firm = 75,000 + 45,000 + 90,000 = Rs. 2,10,000.
Charu's new capital = $2,10,000\times\frac{2}{5}$ = Rs. 84,000.
Cash Charu brings in = 84,000 − 45,000 = Rs. 39,000. Arjun brings in 1,26,000 − 75,000 = Rs. 51,000, and the two amounts together equal the Rs. 90,000 paid to Bela.
Answer: (3)

Arjun, Bina and Chetan share profits in the ratio of 2 : 2 : 1. Bina retires. After all adjustments for reserves and revaluation, her capital account shows a credit balance of Rs. 84,000. Arjun and Chetan agree to pay her Rs. 1,04,000 in full settlement. They will share future profits equally. The firm's goodwill does not appear in the books.

With what amount will Chetan's capital account be debited for Bina's share of goodwill?
questions.explanation:
Given: Bina's adjusted capital is Rs. 84,000 and the lump sum paid is Rs. 1,04,000.
Hidden goodwill (Bina's share) = 1,04,000 − 84,000 = Rs. 20,000.
Gaining share = New share − Old share:
- Arjun = 1/2 − 2/5 = 1/10
- Chetan = 1/2 − 1/5 = 3/10
So the gaining ratio is 1 : 3.
Chetan's debit = 20,000 × 3/4 = Rs. 15,000. Arjun is debited Rs. 5,000.
Rs. 6,667 is wrong because it uses the old ratio 2 : 1. Rs. 10,000 is wrong because it uses the new ratio 1 : 1.
Answer: (2)

How many of the following items are ADDED (credited) while calculating the amount due to a retiring partner?
(a) Credit balance of his current account
(b) His share of general reserve
(c) His drawings up to the date of retirement
(d) Interest on his capital up to the date of retirement
(e) His share of accumulated losses (debit balance of Profit and Loss A/c)
(f) Salary due to him up to the date of retirement
questions.explanation:
(a) Added: a credit balance of the current account is owed to him.
(b) Added: he gets his share of accumulated profits.
(c) Deducted: drawings reduce his claim.
(d) Added: interest on capital is due to him.
(e) Deducted: he must bear his share of accumulated losses.
(f) Added: salary due to him is part of his claim.
So the added items are (a), (b), (d) and (f), which makes 4.
Answer: (3)

questions.explanation:

The Profit and Loss Suspense Account
questions.explanation:
Settling a deceased partner's dues is similar to settling a retiring partner's dues.
The one difference is that the amount credited to the deceased partner is transferred to his Executors' Account. Payment is then made to the executors (legal representatives).
The P&L Suspense Account is wrong. It only records his share of profit for the intervening period and does not hold his total dues.

• Land of Rs. 2,00,000 is appreciated by 15%.
• Stock of Rs. 60,000 is reduced by 10%.
• A provision of 5% is created on debtors of Rs. 80,000 (no existing provision).

questions.question:
Assertion (A): When the amount due to a retiring partner is transferred to his Loan Account, the balance of this account is shown on the liabilities side of the Balance Sheet of the reconstituted firm until the last instalment is paid.
Reason (R): After the transfer, the retiring partner is no longer an owner. The amount payable to him is a debt the firm owes to an outsider.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. The entry is Retiring Partner's Capital A/c Dr. To Retiring Partner's Loan A/c. The loan balance then appears among liabilities until it is fully paid off.
R is true. Once the partner retires, his claim is no longer capital. It becomes an obligation of the firm towards him.
Because the amount is a debt owed to an outsider, it is shown as a liability. So R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)

X, Y and Z share profits in the ratio of 2 : 2 : 1. Y retires, and X and Z decide to share future profits in the ratio of 1 : 2. The goodwill of the firm is valued at Rs. 1,50,000 and does not appear in the books. How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) X sacrifices 1/15 share on Y's retirement.
(ii) Z's Capital Account is debited with Rs. 70,000.
(iii) Y's Capital Account is credited with Rs. 60,000.
(iv) X's Capital Account is debited with Rs. 10,000.

So 3 statements are correct.

options: Interest at 6% p.a. on the amount due until the date of payment, or a share of profits earned with his money, whichever he chooses
Interest at 12% p.a. on the amount due until the date of payment, compulsorily
A share of profits based on the old profit sharing ratio only
Nothing, since he has ceased to be a partner

Given: Kavya's share = $\frac{4}{10}$. It is acquired in the ratio 3 : 1.
Leena acquires $\frac{3}{4} \times \frac{4}{10} = \frac{3}{10}$, and Mohan acquires $\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{4}{10} = \frac{1}{10}$.
Formula: New share = Old share + Acquired share.
Leena = $\frac{3}{10} + \frac{3}{10} = \frac{6}{10}$, and Mohan = $\frac{3}{10} + \frac{1}{10} = \frac{4}{10}$.
So the new ratio is 6 : 4 = 3 : 2. Note that 3 : 1 is the acquisition ratio, not the new ratio.

(ii) Arjun's new share is $\frac{2}{5}$.
(iii) The new profit sharing ratio of Arjun, Chirag and Dev is 2 : 1 : 2.

(v) Debit: a decrease in an asset.

Assertion (A): Before Sonal's share of the current goodwill is adjusted, the existing goodwill of Rs. 48,000 is written off, and Sonal's capital account is also debited with Rs. 16,000.

questions.question: Rohit retires from a firm, and Rs. 2,40,000 is due to him. The partnership deed says nothing about how or when he is to be paid, and the firm has not paid him yet. Under Section 37 of the Indian Partnership Act, 1932, Rohit is entitled to:

either interest at 6% p.a. until the date of payment, or the share of profits earned with his money, at his option
only his share of profits based on the old profit sharing ratio until the date of payment

On a partner's retirement, the following adjustments are agreed. How many of them will be recorded on the DEBIT side of the Revaluation Account?

(ii) Outstanding expenses brought down from Rs. 4,500 to Rs. 3,750
(iii) An unrecorded computer worth Rs. 8,000 brought into the books
(iv) An unrecorded claim for damages of Rs. 5,000 accepted as a liability

(vi) Credit: the liability decreases.

questions.question: Aman, Bharat and Chetan share profits in the ratio of 2 : 2 : 1. Goodwill appears in their books at Rs. 30,000. Bharat retires, and on that date goodwill is valued at Rs. 75,000. Aman and Chetan will share future profits in the ratio of 3 : 2. Considering both entries relating to goodwill, what is the total amount debited to Aman's capital account?
questions.explanation:
Step 1: The existing goodwill is written off among all partners in the old ratio. Aman's share = $30,000\times\frac{2}{5}$ = Rs. 12,000.
Step 2: Bharat's share of goodwill = $75,000\times\frac{2}{5}$ = Rs. 30,000.
Gains: Aman = $\frac{3}{5}-\frac{2}{5}=\frac{1}{5}$ and Chetan = $\frac{2}{5}-\frac{1}{5}=\frac{1}{5}$, so the gaining ratio is 1 : 1.
Aman's debit in Step 2 = Rs. 15,000.
Total debit = 12,000 + 15,000 = Rs. 27,000. Writing off the old goodwill in the new ratio would wrongly give Rs. 33,000.
Answer: (2)

questions.question: Rohan, a partner in a firm, dies during the year. After all adjustments, the balance standing to the credit of his capital account is to be transferred. Which journal entry records this transfer?
